1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

LAC no. 70 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Daya Nand v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 13 Daya Nand Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187994917/

sentences.text: 3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 15/8 (416), 9 (416), 12 (416), 13 (4 16), 14 (416) i.e. total area measuring 24 Bigha in which the share of petitioners no. 1 to 5 is 1/10 each and share of petitioner no. 6 and 7 is 1/4th each, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been arbitrarily assessed by the LAC without taking into account the fertility, potentiality,
surroundings LAC no. 70 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Daya Nand v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 13 and topography under acquisition.

entities.text: Daya Nand v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The said land is levelled land and is situated in a belt which has not experienced any major earthquake, flood or any other natural calamity for the last more than hundred years and is best suited for all sorts of land uses like residential,
commercial, industrial and agricultural etc. the quality of the said land makes it most suitable in the state of Delhi.
6. It is stated that the said land falls in the most fertile belt of Delhi and the petitioners are cultivating the said land and are growing three crops in a year "fasali year".

Whole of the said land is having welldeveloped irrigation system having borwell, tubewells and canal system linked with Yamuna Canal and all crops including cereals, vegetables crops, oil yielding crops and sugarcane are being cultivated by the petitioners and the income per acre is more than Rs. 2 lakhs per year.
In addition to it, the petitioners are having milk yielding cattles which are fully fed by the land produce and all the daily needs of the petitioners are fulfilled by the said land.

7. It is stated that the petitioners shall be forced to change from one mode of life i.e. agro based lifestyle to modern lifestyle due to the acquisition of the said land and the new lifestyle has become more expensive, and the daily inflation shall have an adverse economic effect on the petitioners, who were selfreliant before acquisition of the said land.
The said land acquired by the ld. LAC is surrounded by the residential as LAC no. 70 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Daya Nand v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 13 well as industrial areas.

entities.text: Daya Nand v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The area under acquisition is having mettled roads, and is having a very good connectivity with other areas of Delhi.
The National Highway10 is just 1 km away from the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera and the railway line from Delhi Junction to Firozpur is just half kilometres away.
The infrastructure in the vicinity of the land of the petitioners is already in existence i.e. electricity, schools, residential areas and industrial Daya Nand Ors.

8. It is stated that the land under acquisition including the said land is having better location than the revenue estate of Village like Karala, Savda, Madanpur Dabas, Mundaka, Ghewra and Hiran Koodna, etc which falls on the NorthWestern and SouthWestern side of the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi where sale instances show constant rise in the land rates, however,
those lands are far away from village Rani Khera, if the distance from the urban limits of Delhi state are taken into consideration.

The said land has great potentiality and is fit for supporting high rise buildings, and other residential infrastructure with a lesser investment, if compared with the development work carried out in South Delhi and East Delhi, where the land was hilly, terrain and low line respectively, which require a huge amount for levelling and making the land usable for construction activities.

The ld. LAC has overlooked the facts while determining the market value of the said land, in as much as, if all the factors are taken together for assessing the market value of the land under LAC no. 70 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Daya Nand v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 13 acquisition, it shall be Rs. 1 crore per acre or at least Rs. 2000/ per square yard.

sentences.text: If the said land under acquisition is auctioned to the private developers, they would have purchased the same for more than Rs. 1 crore per acre, which fact finds support from the fact that the land bordering Delhi, particularly in the village Kundli and Kasar in Haryana, has shown a very fast increase in the land prices due to participation of private builders, however, the land of Village Kundli and Kasar is comparatively inferior to the land under acquisition.

9. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming market value of Rs. 2000/ per sq. yards or Rs. 1 crores per acre in addition to the said market value.

The petitioners have also claimed solatium @ 30% and additional amount @ 12% and further claim interest @ 9% from date of award upto 1 year and @
15% thereafter till the date of payment on the enhanced compensation in the interest of justice.

10. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted that the notification under Section 4 was passed on 21.03.2003 and the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 19.03.2004 and the said land has been acquired for the public purposes i.e. for Planned Development of Delhi.

It is submitted that the learned LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view all the aspects and has assessed the market value after considering LAC no. 70 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Daya Nand v.
Union of India Page no. 7 of 13 the level of development, locality and situation of the area where the said land is situated.

The Ld. LAC adopted the indicative price fixed by the Government of NCT of Delhi of land falling in "Block A".

All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

It is submitted that the reference petition is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed as no ground or reason has been shown by the petitioners for enhancement in the market value of the land which were correctly assessed by the learned LAC.

LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

13. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

19. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.

Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
20.
Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

21. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).

This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.

This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
23.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the Daya Nand Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 8 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187994917/
6 aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 24.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: LAC no.
70 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Daya Nand v. Union of India Page no. 12 of 13 (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
25.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
